last_action: BUG-002 resolved; all tasks and validation gates complete

FR-001.title: The feature MUST preserve the Go 1.26 modular-monolith architecture on Wails v2.13.0 and all behavior compatible with `develop` commit `8f306ce42e55b199ada4761d165461e2ebedc8ae`, including feature-003 hacking behavior and feature-004 player-session and control behavior.

FR-002.title: If `develop` advances before implementation, the implementation MUST inventory and preserve compatible newer behavior rather than revert to the recorded baseline.

FR-003.title: Before public transport implementation begins, the project MUST inventory every application-owned public player contract, private desktop payload, known persistence field, and serializable application configuration field.

FR-004.title: Every inventory item MUST be classified as represented by a versioned protobuf contract, governed by a third-party schema, or excluded as a non-serializable implementation dependency.

FR-005.title: The completed inventory MUST contain zero unclassified application-owned structured boundaries and zero unclassified serializable configuration fields.

FR-006.title: Versioned public schemas MUST govern recognition exchange, personalized player state, roles, phases, assignments, controller state, roster availability, terminal content and presentation, navigation, public hacking patterns, typed mutation requests and results, complete snapshots, compound updates, and sound manifests.

FR-007.title: Versioned private schemas MUST govern known session-v1, terminal, recursive content-node, player-config-v1, roster, Wails request, Wails result, status, event, session-operation, player-config-operation, command, coordination, terminal-switch, server-information, runtime-status, and serializable configuration semantics.

FR-008.title: Serializable configuration contracts MUST cover application, player-server, coordination, queue, timeout, path, tunnel, startup, and shutdown values that can cross or be recorded at application-owned boundaries.

FR-009.title: Embedded filesystems, callbacks, event sinks, clocks, random sources, service interfaces, process handles, listeners, and other dependency-injection objects MUST remain excluded from serializable configuration contracts.

FR-010.title: Third-party schemas including `wails.json`, `package.json`, Buf configuration, GitHub Actions workflows, plist files, and third-party traffic-policy formats MUST NOT be duplicated in application protobuf schemas.

FR-011.title: Public and private schemas MUST use separate versioned packages and MUST preserve an inspectable one-way boundary in which public schemas never import private schemas.

FR-012.title: Generated player-client inputs and their transitive bundle MUST contain no private desktop, persistence, native-path, resolved-configuration, tunnel, credential, or private hacking contract.

FR-013.title: Protobuf schema existence MUST NOT authorize public exposure of any message or capability.

FR-014.title: Generated protobuf values MUST remain detached boundary values and MUST NOT become canonical mutable domain, navigation, live, coordination, or hacking aggregates.

FR-015.title: Public transport MUST contain no handwritten JSON envelopes, generic maps, generic command procedure, generic RPC dispatcher, duplicated public transport DTO, or manually maintained RPC router.

FR-016.title: The public player service MUST expose exactly one server-streaming subscription responsibility and separate unary responsibilities for character selection, navigation action, password-or-filler guess, special-pattern activation, and sound-manifest discovery.

FR-017.title: The public service MUST NOT merge player mutations into a generic command procedure.

FR-018.title: Browser-originated mutations MUST use unary procedures and authoritative state delivery MUST use server streaming.

FR-019.title: The browser player MUST NOT require client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming request bodies.

FR-020.title: The player page, generated player procedures, static resources, and sound assets MUST remain same-origin in local and ngrok modes without wildcard CORS.

FR-021.title: The public listener MUST NOT expose runtime status, server information, health, reflection, generic capability discovery, diagnostics, tunnel status, or client-count procedures.

FR-022.title: The public listener MUST NOT expose `ForceHackSuccess`, `ResetFailedHack`, native dialogs, arbitrary file operations, URL opening, tunnel configuration, private candidates, secret words, future outcomes, credentials, raw connection identities, or another session's private information.

FR-023.title: The browser Connect transport MAY use generated protobuf JSON or binary encoding, but planning MUST choose and pin one encoding using official ConnectRPC guidance.

FR-024.title: Recognition handles MUST remain opaque to clients, and clients MUST NOT parse them or infer session identity, age, validity, assignment, presence, controller authority, or any lifecycle state from their contents.

FR-025.title: The Subscribe request MUST use explicit protobuf presence for its recognition-handle scalar so absence is distinguishable from a present empty value.

FR-026.title: A Subscribe request with the recognition handle absent MUST create exactly one process-local logical session and return its opaque handle in the initial complete snapshot.

FR-027.title: A Subscribe request with a present blank, oversized, or structurally malformed recognition handle MUST return Connect `invalid_argument` without creating a logical session or replacement handle.

FR-028.title: A Subscribe request with a currently recognized handle MUST reattach to the same logical session.

FR-029.title: A Subscribe request with a well-formed nonblank handle that is unknown or expired MUST create a fresh logical session, issue a replacement handle, and return a complete current snapshot without restoring expired assignment or controller authority unless existing canonical rules independently establish it.

FR-030.title: A unary request with a missing, blank, oversized, or structurally malformed recognition handle MUST return Connect `invalid_argument`.

FR-031.title: A unary request with a well-formed nonblank handle that is unknown or expired MUST return typed `invalid-session` without creating a logical session or replacement handle and without mutation, revision advancement, random-source advancement, publication, or a replay result for the nonexistent session.

FR-032.title: Recognition-handle validation MUST impose a finite documented semantic bound while preserving handle opacity.

FR-033.title: Concurrent first-time tabs in one browser profile MUST converge on one accepted recognition handle and one logical session.

FR-034.title: Every active stream using one valid handle MUST attach to the same logical session and receive equivalent personalized state.

FR-035.title: Raw displayed browser connection count MUST equal active public server streams.

FR-036.title: Aggregate logical-session presence MUST remain connected while at least one stream for that session remains active.

FR-037.title: Closing a logical session's final stream MUST mark it disconnected without automatically releasing its character claim or controller identity; reconnecting within the same process MUST restore current presence and authoritative assignment, while process restart MUST restore no recognition mapping, logical session, claim, controller, broadcast, revision, live terminal, navigation, hacking, pending action, or replay-cache state.

FR-038.title: The first application message on every new or reconnecting subscription MUST be exactly one complete personalized compound snapshot.

FR-039.title: Every complete snapshot MUST contain the accepted or replacement recognition handle, complete current personalized player state, current authoritative revision, and exactly one terminal-presentation variant.

FR-040.title: The snapshot terminal-presentation variant MUST be either the complete current public live-terminal projection or an explicit no-live-terminal state.

FR-041.title: Snapshot creation MUST never generate or regenerate a hacking puzzle.

FR-042.title: Reconnect snapshots MUST NOT replay ambient transitions, hacking outcome cues, stale actions, or prior accepted actions.

FR-043.title: Stream attachment and snapshot capture MUST form a gap-free boundary such that a snapshot at revision R is followed by no application message at revision R or lower.

FR-044.title: Every relevant committed revision after a subscriber's snapshot MUST be offered once to its affected logical session; every attached physical stream that remains active and responsive through delivery MUST observe that revision exactly once, while a canceled, disconnected, or overflowing stream MAY observe zero messages for it and MUST terminate so recovery can use a new complete snapshot.

FR-045.title: One accepted mutation MUST commit exactly one coordinator revision.

FR-046.title: Each affected logical session MUST be offered exactly once the accepted mutation's single logical compound authoritative update, personalized to contain every public state component changed for that session by the action.

FR-047.title: No physical stream MUST observe the same revision more than once, and every physical stream attached to an affected logical session that remains active and responsive through delivery MUST observe the session's equivalent personalized update exactly once.

FR-048.title: The compound-update contract MUST permit several complete changed player, terminal-presentation, navigation, and hacking projections in one value.

FR-049.title: An omitted compound-update component MUST mean unchanged and MUST NOT act as an ambiguous partial patch.

FR-050.title: A subscriber MUST NOT receive several player, terminal, navigation, or hacking application messages with the same revision.

FR-051.title: Revisions observed by one subscriber after its snapshot MUST be strictly increasing while revisions irrelevant to that personalized projection MAY be skipped.

FR-052.title: Publication MUST permit one committed revision to produce different personalized compound updates for different logical sessions.

FR-053.title: Clients MUST NOT optimistically mutate assignment, role, active terminal, navigation, attempts, logs, patterns, removed duds, puzzle result, or any other canonical shared state.

FR-054.title: An accepted action MUST remain pending until the client has both its correlated unary result and an applicable authoritative stream state at the result revision or a later relevant revision.

FR-055.title: A rejected action MUST clear its correlated pending state immediately.

FR-056.title: Every player mutation MUST validate request structure and finite bounds, recognition handle, live logical session with the required active subscription relationship, request identity, broadcast identity, and action-specific semantic fields before domain mutation.

FR-057.title: Character selection MUST be allowed only for a connected, recognized, currently unassigned logical session; MUST NOT require an existing assignment, controller authority, terminal identity, or hacking generation; MUST reject unavailable, unknown, conflicting, malformed, stale, or duplicate selection attempts without shared-state mutation, except that an exact request whose result remains retained replays only that result without a new effect under FR-062; and MUST preserve the current domain behavior by which acceptance can establish controller ownership.

FR-058.title: Navigation actions, password-or-filler guesses, and special-pattern activation MUST require an assigned, eligible, connected active controller, the applicable current terminal or broadcast identity, and the current hacking generation when generation-bound; requests from unassigned sessions, observers, non-controllers, disconnected sessions, stale broadcasts, stale terminals, or stale generations MUST be rejected without mutation or random-source advancement.

FR-059.title: A rejected, stale, duplicate, structurally invalid, observer-originated, disconnected-controller, or non-actionable request MUST NOT mutate canonical state, increment revision, publish an update, consume an attempt, or consume hacking randomness.

FR-060.title: Replay storage MUST default to 256 request-result records per logical session and broadcast.

FR-061.title: Exact replay MUST be guaranteed only while the matching request-result record remains retained.

FR-062.title: An identical retained request MUST return its original result and revision without another canonical effect.

FR-063.title: A retained request identity reused with a different procedure or payload fingerprint MUST return `duplicate` without mutation.

FR-064.title: Replay-cache eviction MUST be deterministic but MUST NOT be presented as a public protocol guarantee.

FR-065.title: After eviction, cache clearing, logical-session removal, or process restart, a reused request identity MUST be evaluated as new against current state and MAY be accepted if still valid.

FR-066.title: The feature MUST NOT claim broadcast-lifetime or process-lifetime exactly-once behavior after replay-record loss.

FR-067.title: Concurrent activation of one unused current-generation special pattern MUST produce exactly one accepted mutation.

FR-068.title: Randomness consumption MUST be limited to the winning accepted special-pattern activation.

FR-069.title: An accepted special-pattern activation MUST consume one outcome draw and at most one additional dud-selection draw under unchanged feature-003 rules.

FR-070.title: Every stale, used, duplicate, rejected, or losing concurrent special-pattern activation MUST consume zero random calls.

FR-071.title: The feature MUST preserve current pattern probabilities, dud-removal rules, attempts-reset rules, board-generation rules, and opaque generation-bound `patternId` semantics.

FR-072.title: `HACK_ADMIN` MUST remain removed from every public contract, handler, generated client, fixture, and active document.

FR-073.title: Malformed bounded protobuf messages, illegal or missing variants, prohibited required `UNSPECIFIED` enums, a present invalid Subscribe recognition handle, a missing or invalid unary recognition handle, blank or structurally invalid request identity, missing required broadcast or terminal identity, invalid sound category, and structurally invalid action targets MUST return Connect `invalid_argument` before canonical service invocation.

FR-074.title: Every public player RPC, including Subscribe and SoundManifest, MUST enforce a maximum 4 KiB uncompressed protobuf request-message size at the Connect transport or decoding boundary before application adapters or canonical services are invoked; exceeding that limit MUST return Connect `resource_exhausted`.

FR-075.title: Unsupported public services or procedures MUST return Connect `unimplemented`.

FR-076.title: Request or stream cancellation MUST return Connect `canceled`.

FR-077.title: Temporary public service unavailability MUST return Connect `unavailable`.

FR-078.title: Unexpected failures outside authoritative domain rejection MUST return Connect `internal`.

FR-079.title: Decoded structurally valid player mutations rejected by current state or domain rules MUST return a typed authoritative action result.

FR-080.title: Typed action results MUST use only `accepted`, `invalid-session`, `stale-broadcast`, `unassigned`, `not-controller`, `controller-disconnected`, `stale-terminal`, `invalid-action`, `conflict`, or `duplicate` as stable reasons.

FR-081.title: Stale-generation, used-pattern, absent-puzzle, non-actionable-puzzle, solved-puzzle, failed-puzzle, exhausted-puzzle, and well-formed invalid-target rejections MUST use `invalid-action` unless `stale-terminal` is more specific.

FR-082.title: Invalid Basic Auth MUST fail closed with HTTP `401` before player capabilities are reached.

FR-083.title: Public errors MAY include safe correction or retry guidance but MUST NOT expose request bytes, legacy JSON, recognition handles, credentials, native paths, stack traces, private identities, private candidates, secret words, future outcomes, tunnel policy details, or internal dependency errors.

FR-084.title: Wails MUST remain the trusted private desktop transport and MUST preserve its native structured-object transport.

FR-085.title: Every structured Wails request, result, status, and event MUST have a versioned private protobuf semantic contract.

FR-086.title: Explicit typed adapters MUST exhaustively map existing Wails-facing compatibility values, generated private protobuf values, and transport-independent application or domain values.

FR-087.title: Wails-facing compatibility DTOs MUST remain narrow private adapter projections and MUST NOT become reusable public transport models or an independent source of business semantics.

FR-088.title: Adding or changing a private protobuf field or variant without updating its Wails adapter MUST fail verification.

FR-089.title: Wails MAY retain framework-native internal JSON marshalling but MUST NOT carry protobuf binary, Base64, ProtoJSON, serialized protobuf envelopes, or generic maps.

FR-090.title: Existing named Wails methods and events MUST NOT be replaced by a generic protobuf or RPC dispatcher.

FR-091.title: Private business and validation outcomes MUST remain explicit structured result objects rather than ad hoc error strings.

FR-092.title: All private desktop capabilities for sessions, player configurations, roster and logical-session coordination, broadcast control, terminal switching, failed-hack reset, `ForceHackSuccess`, URL opening, runtime status, server information, and desktop events MUST remain available under their current eligibility rules.

FR-093.title: Every frontend-facing private method and event listed in the Verbatim Constraints section MUST preserve its exact name, argument behavior, result behavior, and native JavaScript value or object shape.

FR-094.title: Known `Session`, `Terminal`, recursive `ContentNode`, `PlayerConfig`, and roster fields MUST have protobuf definitions without replacing their established persistence codecs.

FR-095.title: Persisted sessions MUST remain portable JSON version-1 documents and persisted player configurations MUST remain separate strict JSON version-1 documents.

FR-096.title: Neither governed persistence format MUST be replaced by protobuf binary or generic ProtoJSON.

FR-097.title: Session and player-config JSON field names MUST remain exactly compatible with their current version-1 documents.

FR-098.title: Session-compatible unknown fields MUST be preserved at every currently supported level.

FR-099.title: Current persistence validation limits, defaults, selected-path behavior, normalized relative player-config references, ordered save revisions, and atomic-save behavior MUST remain unchanged.

FR-100.title: Player-config decoding MUST continue to reject unknown fields, trailing data, unsupported versions, invalid identities, duplicate identities, and all other current validation failures.

FR-101.title: Runtime recognition, assignments, controller state, broadcasts, revisions, live-terminal runtime, navigation, hacking, pending actions, and replay caches MUST remain absent from durable session and player-config data.

FR-102.title: A roster or association change MUST NOT be published before its required complete-file atomic save succeeds.

FR-103.title: Environment variables and command-line arguments MUST retain their current precedence and validation.

FR-104.title: The player listener MUST retain default port 3690, delivery queue default 32, and current startup-timeout behavior.

FR-105.title: Protected public access MUST retain a provider-assigned public endpoint when no fixed domain is configured, credential-pair validation, and fail-closed Basic Auth.

FR-106.title: Tunnel credentials MUST remain process-local and redacted.

FR-107.title: Credentials MUST be absent from public schemas, runtime status, desktop events, logs, public errors, session files, player-config files, and generated public documentation.

FR-108.title: Private protobuf configuration contracts MUST NOT authorize configuration exposure through public procedures.

FR-109.title: The structured sound-list endpoint MUST be replaced by the typed unary sound-manifest responsibility.

FR-110.title: Sound discovery MUST preserve all current categories and allowlisted extensions listed in Verbatim Constraints.

FR-111.title: A successful sound manifest MUST return the requested allowlisted category and deterministically sorted allowlisted filenames or safe relative asset paths.

FR-112.title: A sound manifest MUST NOT return absolute origins, native filesystem paths, embedded filesystem capabilities, or arbitrary caller-supplied paths.

FR-113.title: The browser MUST resolve sound asset URLs against the current same origin.

FR-114.title: A valid category with a missing, unreadable, or empty folder MUST return an empty successful manifest.

FR-115.title: An absent or `UNSPECIFIED` sound category MUST return `invalid_argument`.

FR-116.title: Sound discovery and prefetch MUST remain asynchronous, optional, and non-blocking.

FR-117.title: Ambient and hacking cues MUST continue to follow newly applied authoritative transitions.

FR-118.title: Reconnect snapshots, stale updates, rejected actions, exact replays, and rerenders MUST NOT replay authoritative outcome cues.

FR-119.title: Static HTML, CSS, fonts, images, generated scripts, and sound files MUST remain ordinary embedded same-origin HTTP resources.

FR-120.title: Packaged operation MUST remain fully offline without a CDN or external development server.

FR-121.title: Every subscriber MUST have bounded buffering.

FR-122.title: A slow, blocked, overflowing, canceled, or disconnected subscriber MUST NOT block canonical mutation, another subscriber, effect publication, detachment, or shutdown.

FR-123.title: Subscriber cancellation, disconnection, or buffer overflow MUST cancel or close only the affected physical stream within bounded time, release its resources, and MUST NOT block canonical mutation, other logical sessions, or sibling physical streams.

FR-124.title: Shutdown MUST cancel streams, release subscribers and logical presence, close the listener, stop tunnel-owned resources, wait for owned workers, and remain idempotent.

FR-125.title: The browser MUST retain the current three-second reconnect delay unless planning documents an equivalent or safer bounded policy.

FR-126.title: Before bulk migration, planning MUST require a thin vertical proof covering generated subscription and snapshot, at least one unary mutation, same-origin local mode, authenticated ngrok mode, Basic Auth failure, and bundled packaged assets.

FR-127.title: Any temporary side-by-side player transport MUST be limited to the migration branch and the period while parity tests are constructed.

FR-128.title: Final acceptance MUST contain exactly one application-owned public player protocol.

FR-129.title: Final cutover MUST remove active WebSocket routes and upgrades, browser `WebSocket` construction, legacy JSON request decoders and envelopes, legacy protocol fixtures, the direct `github.com/coder/websocket` dependency, WebSocket CSP allowances, and active documentation describing the superseded protocol.

FR-130.title: Any retained historical completed feature document MUST mark legacy WebSocket contracts as superseded and non-authoritative.

FR-131.title: The same public schemas MUST generate type-safe Go public handlers and values plus ECMAScript player values and clients.

FR-132.title: Private schemas MUST generate the types required by explicit Wails and persistence adapters without entering the player bundle.

FR-133.title: The Buf CLI, protobuf compiler and generators, ConnectRPC generator, Go runtime packages, ECMAScript runtime packages, and package-manager dependencies MUST be pinned.

FR-134.title: Generated files MUST be deterministic, reproducible, handled according to repository policy, and never manually edited.

FR-135.title: The packaged application MUST contain all required generated and bundled player code.

FR-136.title: Clean development startup MUST remain one root `wails dev` command.

FR-137.title: Contract verification MUST cover formatting, lint, deterministic zero-diff generation, one schema revision for Go and ECMAScript outputs, breaking-change detection, public/private dependency inspection, and exhaustive private adapter mapping.

FR-138.title: Breaking-change checks MUST reject incompatible field-number, field-type, enum, package, and service changes against the committed baseline once it exists.

FR-139.title: Compatible unknown protobuf fields MUST follow standard forward-compatible protobuf behavior while known request fields remain authoritatively validated.

FR-140.title: Removed protobuf fields, mutually exclusive variants, and enum values MUST reserve their former names and numbers as applicable.

FR-141.title: Every protobuf enum MUST define an `UNSPECIFIED` zero value unless the schema imports a well-known type whose governing rules already define its representation.

FR-142.title: Protobuf `optional` MUST be reserved for scalar presence when absence is semantically different from the scalar default.

FR-143.title: Mutually exclusive protobuf payload variants MUST use `oneof`; parallel optional variant fields and string discriminator fields are prohibited.

FR-144.title: Every accepted state-changing action MUST mutate canonical state exactly once, advance the authoritative revision exactly once, produce exactly one logical compound update for the committed revision, and offer it once to each affected logical session before completing the unary response.

FR-145.title: Planning MUST record and tests MUST enforce a finite encoded HTTP-body limit and decompression limit consistent with Connect framing overhead, including compressed requests and messages enlarged with unknown protobuf fields.

FR-146.title: Recognition handles, request identities, broadcast identities, terminal and generation identifiers, pattern identifiers, navigation targets, guesses, and sound categories MUST each have finite semantic limits below the public request-message maximum.

FR-147.title: Sound categories MUST be validated against the existing allowed catalog and MUST NOT accept paths, path fragments, or arbitrary filesystem input.

FR-148.title: Rejection at any public message-size, encoded-body, decompression, structural, finite field-bound, or sound-category boundary check MUST create no logical session, mutation, revision, logical publication, replay entry, or random-source advancement and MUST occur before canonical service invocation.

FR-149.title: The server MUST NOT retry old incremental events as though physical delivery had been acknowledged; a terminated stream MUST recover only by reconnecting to a complete current authoritative snapshot.

intent: Replace handwritten player JSON HTTP/WebSocket contracts with a protobuf-first ConnectRPC API while preserving authoritative gameplay, private Wails behavior, persistence, security, lifecycle, sound, and packaging compatibility.

No persisted live, navigation, hacking, assignment, controller, recognition, pending-action, or replay-cache runtime state.
No exactly-once guarantee after replay-cache eviction or loss.
No session version 2 or player-config version 2.
No replacement of governed JSON files with protobuf binary or generic ProtoJSON.
No gameplay, navigation, hacking, special-pattern, character-selection, controller, or sound redesign.
No separately deployed backend or microservice.
No public exposure of the private Wails bridge or trusted operations.
No protobuf binary, Base64, ProtoJSON, or generic dispatcher through Wails.
No public health, runtime-status, server-information, reflection, capability-discovery, or diagnostic service.

approach: Introduce separate versioned public, private, persistence, and configuration protobuf graphs; generate pinned Go artifacts for all graphs and public-only ECMAScript artifacts; and adapt them at the existing Wails, JSON, and Connect boundaries while keeping control.Service canonical. Prove a same-origin Connect vertical slice before migrating every typed mutation and compound stream, then remove the WebSocket stack completely.

decisions.decision: Use binary Connect transport for the public browser protocol.
decisions.why: It provides generated typed browser/server contracts and the required same-origin streaming path without retaining handwritten JSON envelopes.
decisions.rejected: Connect JSON mode or a custom WebSocket protobuf framing layer.

decisions.decision: Pin Buf CLI v1.72.0, Protocol Buffers v35.0, protobuf-go/protoc-gen-go v1.36.11, Connect-Go/protoc-gen-connect-go v1.20.0, Protobuf-ES/protoc-gen-es v2.13.0, and Connect-ES v2.1.2.
decisions.why: Exact pins make generated output reproducible across local and CI environments.
decisions.rejected: Floating latest versions or checked-in output without a reproducible generation toolchain.

decisions.decision: Separate player.v1, private.v1, persistence.v1, and config.v1 schema graphs, generating ECMAScript only for player.v1.
decisions.why: The import graph becomes an enforceable capability boundary that prevents private or persistence data from entering the browser bundle.
decisions.rejected: One shared schema package or browser generation from every package.

decisions.decision: Expose one PlayerService with server-streaming Subscribe plus typed unary SelectCharacter, Navigate, Guess, ActivatePattern, and SoundManifest procedures.
decisions.why: Distinct request types preserve capability-specific validation and avoid rebuilding a generic command dispatcher.
decisions.rejected: A bidirectional command envelope or one generic mutation procedure.

decisions.decision: Register each bounded physical stream before taking and enqueuing its complete personalized snapshot.
decisions.why: This ordering closes the snapshot-to-live race while retaining the current logical-session identity model.
decisions.rejected: Snapshot first and stream registration afterward.

decisions.decision: Publish one personalized CompoundUpdate per logical session and committed revision.
decisions.why: It preserves the existing copy-on-write commit boundary and lets each browser apply board, coordination, and sound consequences atomically.
decisions.rejected: Independent terminal, navigation, hacking, coordination, and sound messages.

decisions.decision: Limit decoded public request messages to 4096 bytes and encoded HTTP bodies to 8192 bytes, with explicit semantic string and enum bounds.
decisions.why: Layered limits protect decoding and decompression while retaining deterministic validation outcomes.
decisions.rejected: Relying only on server defaults or transport body size.

decisions.decision: Fingerprint deterministic serialized protobuf request bytes for replay idempotency.
decisions.why: Generated request messages provide a stable procedure-specific identity without preserving handwritten JSON canonicalization.
decisions.rejected: Raw HTTP bytes, JSON stringification, or request ID alone.

decisions.decision: Keep native Wails values and compatibility-preserving JSON files as boundary representations, using generated protobuf messages only as internal semantic adapters.
decisions.why: This introduces typed schemas without breaking exact desktop method/event identifiers or persistence compatibility rules.
decisions.rejected: Passing protobuf binary, Base64, or ProtoJSON across Wails or replacing file formats.

decisions.decision: Prove a vertical Connect slice first, then complete a one-protocol cutover that removes all WebSocket code and dependencies.
decisions.why: The slice reduces integration risk while the final gate enforces the specification prohibition on dual production protocols.
decisions.rejected: Permanent WebSocket compatibility or a flag-selectable dual stack.

decisions.decision: Execute T112 before T056 as the browser parity prerequisite
decisions.why: The migrated Playwright client can only establish a generated Connect subscription after the fixture exposes the production-shaped Connect handler and bundled static assets
decisions.rejected: Keep the generated order and retain a temporary WebSocket-only fixture during typed browser parity

decisions.decision: Keep compound client/frontend install and build commands in named frontend npm scripts invoked by Wails
decisions.why: Wails forwards shell operators from configuration as frontend CLI arguments; named scripts package reliably and remain contract-testable
decisions.rejected: Embedding && compound commands directly in wails.json

decisions.decision: Run stream registration inside the coordinator attach transaction after capturing the committed snapshot revision.
decisions.why: This makes snapshot capture, physical-stream registration, and the first later update a single gap-free ordered boundary.
decisions.rejected: Registering the physical stream after AttachSubscription returns, which leaves a mutation gap.

decisions.decision: Build and enqueue one personalized compound update per affected logical session inside coordinator commit.
decisions.why: The transaction owns the authoritative revision and can guarantee exactly-once offers before the unary response.
decisions.rejected: Recomputing updates in individual handlers after commit.

decisions.decision: Represent every structured desktop request, result, status, event, and coordination value in private protobuf and explicit adapters.
decisions.why: Descriptor-driven exhaustiveness tests can then fail on unmapped fields while preserving Wails compatibility shapes.
decisions.rejected: Discarded or partial semantic conversions around compatibility DTOs.

decisions.decision: Emit Connect protocol errors with connect.ErrorWriter at the HTTP boundary.
decisions.why: Oversized and unsupported requests must carry standard Connect resource_exhausted or unimplemented codes before invoking application logic.
decisions.rejected: Bare HTTP status responses from generic body-limit middleware.

decisions.decision: Download checksummed official protoc 35.0 archives into a cache and invoke the verified binary directly.
decisions.why: Generation and CI now share an exact compiler pin and generated files expose auditable v7.35.0 provenance.
decisions.rejected: Using whichever protoc happens to be installed on PATH.

decisions.decision: Use pinned Buf v1.72.0 as the sole protobuf compiler entry point and validate plugin versions plus Buf-generated protoc (unknown) provenance
decisions.why: Buf compiles schemas in process, so a second downloaded Google protoc distribution duplicated compiler ownership and bypassed the checked-in Buf v2 templates
decisions.rejected: Standalone protoc v35.0 download, checksum matrix, direct invocation, and exact protoc v7.35.0 header enforcement

decisions.decision: Use pinned Buf CLI as the sole protobuf compiler entry point and validate plugin provenance while accepting protoc unknown headers
decisions.why: Buf compiles schemas in process and the checked-in Buf v2 templates are the intended reproducible generation boundary
decisions.rejected: Downloading or invoking a separately pinned Google protoc distribution

decisions.decision: Compare generated-tree hashes before the first regeneration and keep a deliberate drift regression in CI
decisions.why: Verification must reject stale or manually edited checked-in artifacts instead of silently overwriting them before comparison
decisions.rejected: Hash only after regeneration, which cannot distinguish a clean checkout from repaired drift

decisions.decision: Enforce test conventions with AST inspection across the exact artifact-named feature scope
decisions.why: AST inspection catches aliased imports and renamed testing parameters without imposing feature-specific cleanup on unrelated legacy packages
decisions.rejected: Text-only grep or repository-wide migration beyond the specified scope

decisions.decision: Remove the unused partial player-state offer seam and narrow ConnectCoordinator
decisions.why: All authoritative stream publications must remain coordinator-assembled compound updates inside the transaction boundary
decisions.rejected: Retaining an unused compatibility path that could reintroduce out-of-transaction partial publication

decisions.decision: Enforce Basic Auth in the player application for every exact configured public Host and launch ngrok without traffic-policy processing
decisions.why: The ngrok traffic-policy engine buffered non-empty Connect server-streaming POST responses even for a non-matching rule; application auth preserves streaming and keeps credentials out of process arguments
